text:
marta: quick check on the eval-run results legend + keyboard shortcuts before we freeze for this sprint. figma: https://www.figma.com/file/uvw111/eval-legend
lee: main thing i saw: legend chips are hard to scan when there are 6+ labels. consider collapsing into a single summary with expand chevron.
omar: agree. also the color contrast for 'regressed' red on dark theme fails 4.5:1. needs stronger saturation or different hue.
zoe: UX question: when users press `k` to focus the scorecard filter, should it open the legend or highlight the first chip? my vote: open and focus the search input so they can filter quickly.
marta: good call. shortcut `k` -> focus filter; `g` then `l` for quick jump to legend (like global nav patterns).
lee: legend expand UX: collapsed state shows counts and an overflow + button `Show all labels (6)`; expands inline. on mobile, switch to modal.
omar: a11y: if we collapse, ensure the summary has `aria-expanded` and the list is reachable by keyboard. also announce when legend updates after running an eval (aria-live polite).
zoe: copy nit: label `No change` feels vague. propose `No regression` or `Stable`? which maps better to user mental model.
marta: metrics team prefers `Stable` (matches their naming in reports). use `Stable` and add tooltip `No significant change from baseline` for clarity.
aria-bot: accessibility-scan: contrast issue flagged for regressed chip on dark theme. Recommend #D62828 -> #C1121F or add 1px white border for separation.
lee: implementation note: use CSS variables for palette so themes switch without hardcoding. also add token for chip-border on dark.
omar: perf note: avoid rendering all 200+ result chips. render a summary with virtualized list inside expanded view.
zoe: i'll update figma + create PR with aria attributes, shortcut docs, and a11y fixes. i'll tag @omar for perf review. thanks!
